outputs: Rewritten recipes adhering to dietary constraints

datasets: 1,254,931 recipes from online recipe websites and existing datasets

changes_made.explanation: Removed 'Paraphrase Generation' as this is content transfer not paraphrasing. Consolidated datasets to single canonical form. Removed duplicate output description.
Consolidated duplicate metrics and normalized ROUGE-L to ROUGE base form
No LLM-as-judge evaluation used in this paper

guideline: 5 judges rate each rewritten recipe on 1-5 scale for ingredient usage, closeness to source, dietary constraint compliance, and overall quality
Head-to-head comparisons between models with pairwise preference judgments

- Ask 5 judges to rate each rewritten recipe on a scale of 1 to 5 on criteria including ingredient usage, closeness to source, dietary constraint, and overall quality; collect head-to-head comparisons between models.
Judges rate rewrites on multiple criteria such as ingredient usage, closeness to source, dietary constraint compliance, and overall quality; also perform pairwise preference judgments.

We ask 5 judges to rate each rewritten recipe on a scale of 1 to 5 on these criteria: a. Ingredient usage, b. Closeness to source, c. Dietary constraint, d. Overall quality. We also collect human judgments on head-to-head comparisons between models.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated redundant guideline descriptions and normalized criteria names

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate but contained duplicates and some minor inaccuracies. The paper focuses on document-level content transfer in the recipe domain with dietary constraints as the control mechanism. Human evaluation was comprehensive with both individual ratings and pairwise comparisons.
